title: KCET 2025 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1, revised per KEA revised key (2025-04-25) for Q14 and Q52

questions.q: Which of the following methods of expressing concentration are unitless?
questions.explanation: Mole fraction (ratio of moles) and mass percent (ratio of masses) are both dimensionless ratios, unlike molality (mol/kg) and molarity (mol/L) which carry units.

questions.q: Select the INCORRECT statement/s from the following: (a) 22 books have infinite significant figures. (b) In the answer of calculation 2.5 × 1.25, has four significant figures. (c) Zero's preceding to first non-zero digit are significant. (d) In the answer of calculation 12.11 + 18.0 + 1.012 has three significant figures
questions.explanation: 2.5×1.25=3.125 should be rounded to 2 significant figures (least precise factor), not four, so (b) is wrong; leading zeros before the first non-zero digit are never significant, so (c) is also wrong; 12.11+18.0+1.012=31.122 rounds to 31.1 (3 sig figs), so (d) is correct. Hence only (b) and (c) are incorrect.

questions.q: Given below are the atomic masses of the elements: Li=7, Na=23, Cl=35.5, K=39, Ca=40, Br=80, Sr=88, I=127, Ba=137 (g mol$^{-1}$). Which of the following doesn't form a triad?
questions.explanation: In a Dobereiner triad the atomic mass of the middle element is the average of the other two; this holds for Li-Na-K, Ba-Sr-Ca and Cl-Br-I, but not for Cl, K, Ca.

questions.q: The change in hybridisation (if any) of the 'Al' atom in the following reaction is: AlCl$_3$ + Cl$^-$ $\rightarrow$ AlCl$_4^-$
options: No change in the hybridisation state
questions.explanation: AlCl$_3$ is trigonal planar (sp$^2$); gaining a Cl$^-$ ion makes AlCl$_4^-$ tetrahedral (sp$^3$), so the hybridisation changes from sp$^2$ to sp$^3$.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct option: List-I (Molecule/ion): (a) NO (b) CO (c) O$_2^-$ (d) O$_2$; List-II (Bond order): (i) 1.5 (ii) 2.0 (iii) 2.5 (iv) 3.0
options: a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
a - i, b - iv, c - iii, d - ii
a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory, NO has bond order 2.5, CO has bond order 3.0, O$_2^-$ (superoxide) has bond order 1.5, and O$_2$ has bond order 2.0: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.q: The electronic configuration of X and Y are given below: X: 1s$^2$ 2s$^2$ 2p$^6$ 3s$^2$ 3p$^3$; Y: 1s$^2$ 2s$^2$ 2p$^6$ 3s$^2$ 3p$^5$. Which of the following is the correct molecular formula and type of bond formed between X and Y?
questions.explanation: X (3p$^3$) is phosphorus (valency 3) and Y (3p$^5$) is chlorine (valency 1); both are non-metals, so they form the covalent compound XY$_3$ (PCl$_3$).

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Types of redox reactions): (a) Combination reaction (b) Decomposition reaction (c) Displacement reaction (d) Disproportionation reaction; List-II (Examples): (i) Cl$_2$(g) + 2Br$^-$(aq) $\rightarrow$ 2Cl$^-$(aq) + Br$_2$(l) (ii) 2H$_2$O$_2$(aq) $\rightarrow$ 2H$_2$O(l) + O$_2$(g) (iii) CH$_4$(g) + 2O$_2$(g) $\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ CO$_2$(g) + 2H$_2$O(l) (iv) 2H$_2$O(l) $\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ 2H$_2$(g) + O$_2$(g). Choose the correct answer.
options: a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
a - iv, b - iii, c - i, d - ii
a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
questions.explanation: Combustion of methane (iii) is a combination reaction, electrolysis of water (iv) is decomposition, the halogen displacement (i) is a displacement reaction, and disproportionation of H$_2$O$_2$ (ii) is a disproportionation reaction: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.q: In the following pairs, the one in which both transition metal ions are colourless is
questions.explanation: Sc$^{3+}$ (3d$^0$) and Zn$^{2+}$ (3d$^{10}$) have no unpaired d-electrons available for d-d transitions, so both are colourless.

questions.q: In the reaction between hydrogen sulphide and acidified permanganate solution,
options: H$_2$S is oxidised to S, MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to Mn$^{2+}$
H$_2$S is reduced to S, MnO$_4^-$ is oxidised to Mn$^{2+}$
H$_2$S is oxidised to SO$_2$, MnO$_4^-$ is reduced to MnO$_2$
H$_2$S is reduced to SO$_2$, MnO$_4^-$ is oxidised to Mn$^{2+}$
questions.explanation: Sulphur in H$_2$S is oxidised from -2 to 0 (forming S), while Mn in MnO$_4^-$ is reduced from +7 to +2 (forming Mn$^{2+}$).

questions.q: A member of the Lanthanoid series which is well known to exhibit +4 oxidation state is
questions.explanation: Cerium readily loses its single 4f electron in addition to the two 6s electrons to attain a stable [Xe]4f$^0$ configuration, giving a well-known +4 oxidation state.

questions.q: In which of the following pairs, both the elements do not have (n - 1)$d^{10}$ ns$^2$ configuration?
questions.explanation: Ag (4d$^{10}$5s$^1$) and Cu (3d$^{10}$4s$^1$) both have an ns$^1$, not ns$^2$, outer configuration, so neither has (n-1)d$^{10}$ns$^2$.

questions.q: A ligand which has two different donor atoms and either of the two ligates with the central metal atom/ion in the complex is called ________
questions.explanation: An ambidentate ligand (e.g. NO$_2^-$, SCN$^-$) has two different donor atoms but coordinates through only one of them at a time.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are true about [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$? (a) The complex has tetrahedral geometry. (b) Co-ordination number of Ni is 2 and oxidation state is +4. (c) The complex is sp$^3$ hybridised (d) It is a high spin complex. (e) The complex is paramagnetic.
questions.explanation: [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ has Ni$^{2+}$ (d$^8$) with coordination number 4 and oxidation state +2, so (b) is false; the complex is tetrahedral, sp$^3$ hybridised, high spin and paramagnetic, giving statements a, c, d and e.

questions.q: Which formula and its name combination is incorrect?
questions.explanation: CO$_3^{2-}$ acting as a ligand is named 'carbonato', not 'carbonyl' (which refers to CO), so the name in option 4 (originally keyed) is incorrect; however, option 1's name 'chloridonitrito' also mixes up the naming convention (should be nitrito-O or nitrito-N specified consistently), so KEA's revised key accepted both option 1 and option 4.

questions.q: In the complex ion [Fe(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$]$^{3-}$, the co-ordination number of Fe is
questions.explanation: Oxalate (C$_2$O$_4^{2-}$) is a bidentate ligand, so three oxalate ions occupy 3×2=6 coordination positions around Fe.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II for the reaction pattern: Glucose $\xrightarrow{\text{Reagent}}$ Product → Structural prediction. List-I (Reagents): (a) Acetic anhydride (b) Bromine water (c) Hydroiodic acid (d) Hydrogen cyanide; List-II (Structural prediction): (i) Glucose has an aldehyde group (ii) Glucose has a straight chain of six carbon atoms (iii) Glucose has five hydroxyl groups (iv) Glucose has a carbonyl group. Choose the correct answer.
options: a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
a - iii, b - i, c - ii, d - iv
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
questions.explanation: Acetylation with acetic anhydride (forming the pentaacetate) shows glucose has five -OH groups (a-iii); bromine water oxidises only the aldehyde, showing an aldehyde group (b-i); reduction with HI gives n-hexane, showing a straight chain of six carbons (c-ii); HCN adds to the carbonyl carbon, showing a carbonyl group (d-iv).

questions.q: The correct sequence of α-amino acid, hormone, vitamin, carbohydrate respectively is
options: Aspartic acid, Insulin, Ascorbic acid, rhamnose
questions.explanation: Aspartic acid is an α-amino acid, insulin is a (protein) hormone, ascorbic acid is vitamin C, and rhamnose is a carbohydrate -- correctly matching each category.

questions.q: Which examples of carbohydrates exhibit α-link (α-glycosidic link) in their structure?
questions.explanation: Both components of starch, amylose and amylopectin, are joined by α-glycosidic linkages, unlike cellulose which has β-linkages.

questions.q: In the titration of potassium permanganate (KMnO$_4$) against Ferrous ammonium sulphate (FAS) solution, dilute sulphuric acid but not nitric acid is used to maintain acidic medium, because
options: Nitric acid is a weak acid than sulphuric acid
It is difficult to identify the end point
Nitric acid doesn't act as an indicator
Nitric acid itself is an oxidising agent
questions.explanation: Nitric acid is itself an oxidising agent and would oxidise Fe$^{2+}$ independently of KMnO$_4$, interfering with the redox titration.

questions.q: The group reagent NH$_4$Cl(s) and aqueous NH$_3$ will precipitate which of the following ion?
questions.explanation: NH$_4$Cl/NH$_3$ provides just enough OH$^-$ to exceed the low solubility product of Al(OH)$_3$, precipitating Al$^{3+}$ while Ca$^{2+}$ and Ba$^{2+}$ remain in solution.

questions.q: In the preparation of sodium fusion extract, the purpose of fusing organic compound with a piece of sodium metal is to
options: Decrease the melting point of the compound
Convert the organic compound into vapour state
Convert the elements of the compound from covalent form to ionic form
Convert the elements of the compound from ionic form to covalent form
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Fusion with sodium converts covalently bonded N, S, halogens etc. in the organic compound into ionic sodium salts (NaCN, Na$_2$S, NaX) that can be tested in aqueous solution.

questions.q: The sodium fusion extract is boiled with concentrated nitric acid while testing for halogens. By doing so, it
options: decomposes Na$_2$S and NaCN, if formed
increases the concentration of NO$_3^-$ ion
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Boiling with conc. HNO$_3$ decomposes any Na$_2$S or NaCN formed, which would otherwise interfere with the silver nitrate test for halides.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an aromatic compound? [Structures shown: (1) cyclopentadienyl anion, a five-membered ring bearing a negative charge; (2) a six-membered ring cation drawn with only two double bonds and a positive charge, not fully conjugated around the ring; (3) tropylium cation, a seven-membered ring bearing a positive charge; (4) phenanthrene, three fused benzene rings]
options: Six-membered ring cation shown with only two double bonds (not fully conjugated)
questions.explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion, tropylium cation and phenanthrene are all fully conjugated cyclic systems with 4n+2 π-electrons (aromatic); the six-membered ring cation shown is not fully conjugated and does not satisfy Hückel's rule, so it is non-aromatic.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of the given organic compound is HC$\equiv$C-CH=CH-CH=CH$_2$
questions.explanation: Numbering from either end gives the same locant set {1,3,5} for the multiple bonds; when locant sets tie, the double bond ('ene', cited first) is given the lower locants, so numbering from the CH$_2$ end gives hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne.

questions.q: Among the following, identify the compound that is not an isomer of hexane. [Structures: (1) CH$_3$-CH(CH$_3$)-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_3$; (2) CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CH(CH$_3$)-CH$_2$-CH$_3$; (3) CH$_3$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_2$-CH$_3$; (4) a four-membered ring (cyclobutane) with an ethyl substituent, i.e. ethylcyclobutane]
options: Ethylcyclobutane (a cyclobutane ring with an ethyl substituent)
questions.explanation: Options 1-3 are all branched or straight-chain isomers of hexane (C$_6$H$_{14}$); ethylcyclobutane is a cyclic compound with formula C$_6$H$_{12}$, so it is not an isomer of hexane.

questions.q: The organic compound [a benzene ring with a -C(CH$_3$)$_2$Cl group attached to it] can be classified as ________
questions.explanation: The halogen-bearing carbon is attached directly to the benzene ring but is itself sp$^3$ (not part of the ring), which is the defining feature of a benzylic halide.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene reacts with bromine gas in the presence of Anhyd. AlBr$_3$ to yield p-Bromochlorobenzene. This reaction is classified as ____
questions.explanation: AlBr$_3$ generates an electrophilic Br$^+$ species that substitutes a ring hydrogen on chlorobenzene, a classic electrophilic aromatic substitution.

questions.q: The organometallic compound (CH$_3$)$_3$CMgBr on reaction with D$_2$O produces ____
questions.explanation: Grignard reagents react with D$_2$O by deuterolysis of the C-Mg bond, replacing -MgBr with -D to give (CH$_3$)$_3$CD.

questions.q: The major product formed when 1-Bromo-3-chlorocyclobutane reacts with metallic sodium in dry ether is [structures shown: (1) bromocyclobutane; (2) chlorocyclobutane; (3) plain cyclobutane; (4) a bicyclic structure -- a cyclobutane ring with an extra diagonal bond across it, i.e. bicyclo[1.1.0]butane]
questions.explanation: Intramolecular Wurtz-type coupling (Freund reaction) of the two halogens on the same ring with sodium forms a new C-C bond across the ring, giving the fused bicyclic product bicyclo[1.1.0]butane.

questions.q: Ethyl alcohol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at 413 K. The major product formed is
questions.explanation: At the lower temperature of 413 K, conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ promotes intermolecular dehydration of ethanol to give diethyl ether; dehydration to ethene requires the higher temperature of about 443 K.

questions.q: Phenol can be distinguished from propanol by using the reagent
questions.explanation: Phenol reacts with bromine water to give an immediate white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol, whereas propanol does not react with bromine water.

questions.q: Match the following with their pKa values: Acid: (I) Phenol (II) p-Nitrophenol (III) Ethyl alcohol (IV) Picric acid; pKa: (a) 16 (b) 0.78 (c) 10 (d) 7.1
options: I - b, II - a, III - d, IV - c
I - c, II - d, III - a, IV - b
I - a, II - d, III - c, IV - b
I - a, II - b, III - c, IV - d
questions.explanation: Ethanol (pKa≈16) is least acidic, phenol (pKa≈10) is more acidic, the electron-withdrawing nitro group makes p-nitrophenol more acidic (pKa≈7.1), and the three nitro groups in picric acid make it strongly acidic (pKa≈0.78): I-c, II-d, III-a, IV-b.

questions.q: CH$_3$-C(CH$_3$)$_2$-OCH$_3$ + HI $\rightarrow$ A + B. A and B respectively are
questions.explanation: Cleavage of this tertiary alkyl methyl ether by HI proceeds via S$_N$1 at the more stable tertiary carbocation, giving tert-butyl iodide and methanol (A = CH$_3$OH, B = tert-butyl iodide).

questions.q: Oxidation of Toluene with chromyl chloride followed by hydrolysis gives Benzaldehyde. This reaction is known as ________
questions.explanation: Oxidation of a methylbenzene using CrO$_2$Cl$_2$ (chromyl chloride) followed by hydrolysis to give the aldehyde directly is called the Etard reaction.

questions.q: Statement-I: Reduction of ester by DIBAL-H followed by hydrolysis gives aldehyde. Statement-II: Oxidation of benzyl alcohol with aqueous KMnO$_4$ leads to the formation of Benzaldehyde. Among the above statements, identify the correct statement.
options: Both statements-I and II are true
Both statements-I and II are false
Statement-I is true but statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but statement-II is true
questions.explanation: DIBAL-H at low temperature reduces esters to aldehydes on hydrolysis (Statement-I true); but the strong oxidant KMnO$_4$ over-oxidises benzyl alcohol all the way to benzoic acid, not benzaldehyde (Statement-II false).

questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in their decreasing order of reactivity towards Nucleophilic addition reaction. CH$_3$COCH$_3$, CH$_3$COC$_2$H$_5$, CH$_3$CHO
questions.explanation: Reactivity towards nucleophilic addition decreases with increasing steric bulk and decreasing positive charge on the carbonyl carbon, so aldehyde > methyl ketone > ethyl ketone: CH$_3$CHO > CH$_3$COCH$_3$ > CH$_3$COC$_2$H$_5$.

questions.q: Which of the following has most acidic Hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Each additional electron-withdrawing chlorine on the α-carbon further stabilises the carboxylate anion inductively, so trichloroacetic acid is the most acidic of the four.

questions.q: Which of the following reagents are suitable to differentiate Aniline and N-methylaniline chemically?
options: Conc. Hydrochloric acid and anhydrous zinc chloride
questions.explanation: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test with chloroform and alcoholic KOH gives a foul-smelling isocyanide only with primary amines like aniline; the secondary amine N-methylaniline does not respond, so it distinguishes the two.

questions.q: Which of the following reaction/s does not yield an amine? I. R-X + NH$_3$(alc) $\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ (Hofmann's ammonolysis); II. R-C$\equiv$N with H$_2$/Ni or Na(Hg)/C$_2$H$_5$OH; III. R-C$\equiv$N + H$_2$O $\xrightarrow{H^+}$; IV. R-CO-NH$_2$ + 4[H] via i) LiAlH$_4$ ii) H$_3$O$^+$
questions.explanation: Reaction III is acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile, which yields a carboxylic acid (not an amine); reactions I, II and IV (ammonolysis, nitrile reduction, and LiAlH$_4$ reduction of an amide) all give amines.

questions.q: Match the compounds given in List-I with the items given in List-II: List-I: (I) Benzenesulphonyl Chloride (II) Sulphanilic acid (III) Alkyl Diazonium salts (IV) Aryl Diazonium salts; List-II: (a) Zwitterion (b) Hinsberg reagent (c) Dyes (d) Conversion to alcohols
options: I - b, II - a, III - d, IV - c
I - c, II - b, III - a, IV - d
I - a, II - c, III - b, IV - d
I - c, II - a, III - d, IV - b
questions.explanation: Benzenesulphonyl chloride is the Hinsberg reagent (I-b); sulphanilic acid exists as a zwitterion (II-a); alkyl diazonium salts are unstable and decompose to alcohols (III-d); aryl diazonium salts undergo coupling to form azo dyes (IV-c).

questions.q: The number of orbitals associated with 'N' shell of an atom is
questions.explanation: The N shell has principal quantum number n=4, and the total number of orbitals in a shell is n$^2$ = 16.

questions.q: According to the Heisenberg's Uncertainty principle, the value of $\Delta v.\Delta x$ for an object whose mass is 10$^{-6}$kg is (h = 6.626×10$^{-34}$Js)
questions.explanation: $\Delta v.\Delta x \ge \dfrac{h}{4\pi m} = \dfrac{6.626\times10^{-34}}{4\pi\times10^{-6}} \approx 5.2\times10^{-29}$ (SI units).

questions.q: Given below are two statements. Statement-I: Adiabatic work done is positive when work is done on the system and internal energy of the system increases. Statement-II: No work is done during free expansion of an ideal gas. Choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
questions.explanation: By the IUPAC sign convention, work done on the system is positive and raises internal energy (Statement-I true); free expansion occurs against zero external pressure, so no work is done (Statement-II true).

questions.q: Which one of the following reactions has $\Delta H = \Delta U$?
questions.explanation: $\Delta H = \Delta U$ when the change in the number of gaseous moles is zero; only 2HI(g)⇌H$_2$(g)+I$_2$(g) has $\Delta n_g = 2-2 = 0$.

questions.q: Identify the incorrect statements among the following: (a) All enthalpies of fusion are positive. (b) The magnitude of enthalpy change does not depend on the strength of the intermolecular interactions in the substance undergoing phase transformations. (c) When a chemical reaction is reversed, the value of $\Delta_rH^\circ$ is reversed in sign. (d) The change in enthalpy is dependent of path between initial state (reactants) and final state (products) (e) For most of the ionic compounds, $\Delta_{sol}H^\circ$ is negative.
questions.explanation: Statement (b) is false because enthalpy change does depend on the strength of intermolecular forces; (d) is false because enthalpy is a state function, independent of path; (e) is false since the enthalpy of solution of many ionic compounds is actually positive; so b, d and e are incorrect.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are true about equilibrium? (a) Equilibrium is possible only in a closed system at a given temperature (b) All the measurable properties of the system remain constant at equilibrium. (c) Equilibrium constant for the reverse reaction is the inverse of the equilibrium constant for the reaction in the forward direction.
questions.explanation: All three statements correctly describe features of chemical equilibrium: it requires a closed system at constant temperature, measurable properties stay constant, and K(reverse) = 1/K(forward).

questions.q: According to Le Chatelier's principle, in the reaction CO(g) + 3H$_2$(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ CH$_4$(g) + H$_2$O(g), the formation of methane is favoured by (a) increasing the concentration of CO (b) increasing the concentration of H$_2$O (c) decreasing the concentration of CH$_4$ (d) decreasing the concentration of H$_2$
questions.explanation: Increasing a reactant (CO) or removing a product (CH$_4$) both shift the equilibrium forward, favouring methane formation, so (a) and (c) are correct.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant at 298K for the reaction A + B $\rightleftharpoons$ C + D is 100. If the initial concentrations of all the four species were 1M each, then equilibrium concentration of D (in mol L$^{-1}$) will be
questions.explanation: Letting x be the extent of reaction, $K_c = \dfrac{(1+x)^2}{(1-x)^2} = 100 \Rightarrow \dfrac{1+x}{1-x}=10 \Rightarrow x = 0.818$, so [D] = 1 + x = 1.818 M.

questions.q: Among the following 0.1 m aqueous solutions, which one will exhibit the lowest boiling point elevation, assuming complete ionization of the compounds in solution?
questions.explanation: Boiling point elevation is proportional to the van't Hoff factor i; NaCl gives i=2, the smallest among NaCl(2), AlCl$_3$(4), Al$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$(5) and K$_2$SO$_4$(3), so it shows the lowest elevation.

questions.q: Variation of solubility with temperature T for a gas in liquid is shown by the following graphs. The correct representation is [graphs of Solubility vs T: (1) an increasing straight line, (2) a constant/flat line, (3) a curve rising then falling (peak), (4) a decreasing straight line]
options: Solubility rises then falls with T
questions.explanation: The solubility of a gas in a liquid decreases with increasing temperature (dissolution of gases is exothermic), so the correct graph is a decreasing curve.

questions.q: 180g of glucose, C$_6$H$_{12}$O$_6$, is dissolved in 1 kg of water in a vessel. The temperature at which water boils at 1.013 bar is _____ (given, K$_b$ for water is 0.52 K kg mol$^{-1}$. Boiling point for pure water is 373.15 K)
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose = 180/180 = 1 mol, so molality = 1 mol/kg; $\Delta T_b = K_b m = 0.52\times1 = 0.52$ K, giving a boiling point of 373.15 + 0.52 = 373.67 K.

questions.q: If N$_2$ gas is bubbled through water at 293 K, how many moles of N$_2$ gas would dissolve in 1 litre of water? Assume that N$_2$ exerts a partial pressure of 0.987 bar. [Given K$_H$ for N$_2$ at 293 K is 76.48 K bar]
questions.explanation: By Henry's law, mole fraction x = p/K$_H$ = 0.987/76480 ≈ 1.29×10$^{-5}$; with 1 L water ≈ 55.5 mol, moles of N$_2$ ≈ x × 55.5 ≈ 7.16×10$^{-4}$ mol (option 4); KEA's revised key also accepted option 2 (0.716×10$^{-3}$ = 7.16×10$^{-4}$, the same value written differently).

questions.q: The correct statement/s about Galvanic cell is/are (a) Current flows from cathode to anode (b) Anode is positive terminal (c) If E$_{cell}$ < 0, then it is spontaneous reaction (d) Cathode is positive terminal
questions.explanation: In a galvanic cell the cathode is the positive terminal and conventional current flows externally from the cathode (+) to the anode (-); the anode is negative (not positive), and a reaction is spontaneous only when E$_{cell}$ > 0, so statements (a) and (d) are correct.

questions.q: The electronic conductance depends on
options: The number of valence electrons per atom
questions.explanation: Electronic conductance (in metals) arises from the movement of valence electrons, so it depends on the number of valence electrons per atom; the other options affect ionic conductance instead.

questions.q: For a given half cell, Al$^{3+}$ + 3e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Al on increasing the concentration of aluminium ion, the electrode potential will
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation, $E = E^\circ - \dfrac{RT}{3F}\ln\dfrac{1}{[Al^{3+}]}$, so increasing [Al$^{3+}$] increases the electrode potential.

questions.q: Match the following and select the correct option for the quantity of electricity, in Cmol$^{-1}$, required to deposit various metals at cathode. List-I: (a) Ag$^+$ (b) Mg$^{2+}$ (c) Al$^{3+}$ (d) Ti$^{4+}$; List-II: (i) 386000 Cmol$^{-1}$ (ii) 289500 Cmol$^{-1}$ (iii) 96500 Cmol$^{-1}$ (iv) 193000 Cmol$^{-1}$
options: a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
a - iii, b - iv, c - ii, d - i
a - iv, b - iii, c - i, d - ii
questions.explanation: The charge needed equals n times the Faraday constant (96500 C): Ag$^+$ needs 1F=96500 (iii), Mg$^{2+}$ needs 2F=193000 (iv), Al$^{3+}$ needs 3F=289500 (ii), Ti$^{4+}$ needs 4F=386000 (i).

questions.q: Catalysts are used to increase the rate of a chemical reaction. Because it
options: Increases the activation energy of the reaction
Decreases the activation energy of the reaction
Brings about improper orientation of reactant molecules
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, thereby increasing the rate of reaction.

questions.q: Half-life of a first order reaction is 20 seconds and initial concentration of reactant is 0.2M. The concentration of reactant left after 80 seconds is
questions.explanation: 80 seconds corresponds to 80/20 = 4 half-lives, so the concentration remaining is 0.2/2$^4$ = 0.0125 M.

questions.q: In the given graph [potential energy vs reaction coordinate, showing activation energy E$_a$=215 kJ for the forward reaction and $\Delta H$=90 kJ, an exothermic reaction with products lower in energy than reactants], E$_a$ for the reverse reaction will be
questions.explanation: Since the reaction is exothermic with $\Delta H = 90$ kJ, $E_a(\text{reverse}) = E_a(\text{forward}) - \Delta H = 215 - 90 = 125$ kJ.

questions.q: For the reaction 2N$_2$O$_5$(g) $\rightarrow$ 4NO$_2$(g) + O$_2$(g), initial concentration of N$_2$O$_5$ is 2.0 mol L$^{-1}$ and after 300 min, it is reduced to 1.4 mol L$^{-1}$. The rate of production of NO$_2$ (in mol L$^{-1}$min$^{-1}$) is
questions.explanation: Rate of consumption of N$_2$O$_5$ = (2.0-1.4)/300 = 2×10$^{-3}$ mol L$^{-1}$min$^{-1}$; since NO$_2$ forms at twice the rate of N$_2$O$_5$ consumption (from stoichiometry), rate of production of NO$_2$ = 2×(2×10$^{-3}$) = 4×10$^{-3}$ mol L$^{-1}$min$^{-1}$.
